paper_design_summary: Two online experiments each analyzed 204 paid participants with LLM experience, randomly assigning individuals in a 2 x 2 between-participants design crossing task complexity with partner type or LLM response type (pp. 4-5; Figs. 2 and 4). Experiment 1 compared a scripted feed of ERNIE Bot ideas (5 every 100 s) with a research assistant supplying human-written ideas; Experiment 2 compared batch-responsive and constrained-responsive LLM feeds (10 or 2 ideas per response, 30 ideas in total), during creative-uses-for-a-tire and VR-glasses feature tasks (pp. 3-5). Two experts rated participants' ideas from the 10-minute task for overall novelty and usefulness (1-5) and creative fixation (similarity to LLM ideas, 0-2), with overall scores for each participant's ideas (p. 5); overlap between the experiments' participants is not stated.

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper prints 204 as the number recruited and says the participants were randomly assigned (p. 4). participants.locator: p. 4, Procedure, Experiment 1; p. 6, Fig. 2 caption (N = 204)

ai_tool.name_model: ERNIE Bot (Baidu); ideas generated in advance and posted by the authors' own collaboration system
ai_tool.how_used: The LLM partner followed a script. Every 100 s it posted 5 ideas drawn at random from a pool of 50 ideas that ERNIE Bot had generated in advance, six responses (30 ideas) in the 10-minute task. Participants read the ideas in the chat and submitted their own ideas in a text box. The paper says the LLM partners 'responded six times in total', so participants got no LLM output beyond the script, and it lists letting people decide when LLM outputs are generated as future research (p. 8). It does not say whether participants could type messages to the LLM.

task.description: Two tasks, one per complexity level, assigned at random. Simple task: propose creative uses for a tire, an alternative uses test (divergent_test). Complex task: propose innovative feature points and solutions for an enterprise's product, VR glasses (idea_generation). Participants had 10 minutes to generate as many ideas as possible. task.type holds one value: contrasts within the simple task are divergent_test, contrasts within the complex task are idea_generation, and pooled contrasts mix both.

outcomes.name: Expert-rated creativity of the participant's ideas (overall novelty and usefulness)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two trained, independent external experts, blind to demographics, hypotheses, and design, rated each idea on overall novelty and usefulness on a 5-point scale (1 = extremely low, 5 = extremely high). ICC = 0.847. Their average is the overall creativity score for each participant's ideas (p. 5). The paper calls it the 'objective creativity score'. Analyzed by one-way ANOVA and t-test on partner type and by 2 x 2 ANOVA with simple effects.

outcomes.name: Expert-rated creative fixation (similarity of the participant's ideas to the ideas already generated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts independently rated each idea's overall similarity to the ideas already generated by the LLM on a 3-point scale (0 = copies no keyword or idea; 1 = copies a keyword or idea but expands or modifies it; 2 = nearly copies an existing one). ICC = 0.885. Their average is the creative fixation score for each participant's ideas (p. 5). Higher means more fixation. It compares one person's ideas with the partner's ideas and does not compare different people's outputs, so it is not a diversity measure. It is the mediator in a moderated parallel mediation model with 10,000 bootstrap replications. The text calls it 'creativity fixation' and the figures 'creative fixation'. The paper does not say how the scale was applied in the human-partner arms.

contrasts.reported: LLM partner (vs human partner) on creativity fixation in complex tasks: beta = 1.449, SE = 0.154, P < 0.001 (SEs bootstrapped with 10,000 replications). Higher = more fixation. For context, indirect effects on creativity through fixation (these are not effects on fixation): complex task omega_M1 = -0.322, 95% CI (-0.536, -0.120); index of moderated mediation omega_M1 = -0.319, 95% CI (-0.551, -0.118).
contrasts.locator: p. 6, Results, Experiment 1, Moderated mediation; p. 6, Fig. 3; regressions in Supplementary Table S7 (not in this PDF)

contrasts.reported: Fig. 3 path from LLM partner (versus human partner) to creative fixation: beta = 0.013, P = 0.935 (the parenthesized complex-task value is beta = 1.449, P < 0.001). No SE is printed for the simple-task path. For context, the indirect effect on creativity through fixation in simple tasks: omega_M1 = -0.003, 95% CI (-0.044, 0.045).

eligibility.reason: Both experiments meet all three criteria. Individuals were randomly assigned in online 2 x 2 between-participants designs (p. 4, Experiment 1, Participants and procedures; p. 5, Experiment 2, Participants and procedures). Experiment 1 compares supplied ERNIE Bot ideas with a human partner whose room excludes the LLM (ai_vs_active; p. 3, Study materials); Experiment 2 compares batch-responsive and constrained-responsive delivery of LLM ideas (ai_design; pp. 3 and 5). Each experiment independently analyzes 204 people (p. 6, Fig. 2; p. 7, Fig. 4), meeting the threshold without combining samples. Experts rated the novelty and usefulness of participants' own ideas produced during assistance (p. 5, Measurements for both experiments), satisfying the output criterion independently of self-reports. The main article does not establish whether the experiments share participants; this affects sample dependence, not eligibility. Arm counts remain null because they are absent from the main article and the external supplement could not be checked. Disputed statistical values remain as printed and require clarification before effect extraction.

one_line_finding: With 204 people analyzed per experiment, an LLM partner posting ERNIE Bot ideas raised expert-rated creativity over a scripted human partner on the simple task (2.549 vs 2.182, F(1,200) = 17.152, P < 0.001) and scored lower on the complex task (2.351 vs 2.441, F(1,200) = 1.021, printed with P = 0.028), while two ideas per response instead of ten raised complex-task creativity (2.520 vs 2.139) and lowered simple-task creativity (2.171 vs 2.466) (pp. 5 and 7).
open_questions: Experiment 1 complex-task creativity (p. 5): F(1,200) = 1.021 is printed with P = 0.028 and partial eta^2 = 0.005. These statistics are inconsistent, and P = 0.028 repeats the partner main-effect P. The correct complex-task significance result needs author clarification; no replacement value is inferred.

The creativity cell dispersions are labeled 's.d.' in the text: Experiment 1 prints '0. 62' and '0.63' (p. 5), and Experiment 2 prints '0. 048' and '0.047' (p. 7). Figs. 2 and 4 label their error bars s.e.m. Participant-level SDs and any decimal or labeling errors need verification from posted data; Supplementary Tables S5-S6 are described only as demographic tables.

Experiment 1 pooled creativity: d = -0.301 appears beside 95% CI (-0.266, -0.012), which does not contain d (p. 5). The paper does not specify whether this interval, or the self-reported creativity interval (0.2449, 0.7074), estimates the raw difference or the standardized effect. Authors need to identify the estimand.

Experiment 2 fixation mediation: the index is printed as omega_M1 = -0.319, 95% CI (-0.551, -0.118), but described as 'significant and positive' (p. 7). The same numbers appear for Experiment 1 (p. 6). The correct index and interval require author clarification.

Randomized and analyzed counts in each of the four arms per experiment are absent from the main article. Supplementary Tables S5-S6 describe demographics by condition and may provide counts (pp. 4-5); they have not been checked, so all arm counts remain null.

Experiment 1: how creative fixation was scored in human-partner arms is not stated. The scale refers to similarity to 'the ideas already generated by LLM' (p. 5, Measurements), although the LLM is excluded from the human-partner rooms (p. 3, Study materials). Authors need to identify the reference ideas used by raters.

Whether participants could type messages to ERNIE Bot is not stated. LLM responses followed a fixed script and schedule (p. 3); Supplementary Section S5 may specify the available chat interactions (pp. 4-5).

Whether any participant took part in both experiments is not stated. Each experiment reports 204 participants and different demographics (pp. 4-5), which does not establish separate recruitment or non-overlapping samples. Authors need to confirm sample overlap; a combined unique-person total is unknown.

Primary-contrast extraction: Experiment 1 prints pooled arm means and SDs without arm counts (p. 5); task-specific dispersions are labeled ambiguously, and Experiment 2 supplies no pooled arm means (pp. 6-7). Posted participant data are needed for missing counts and dispersion information. Choosing primary records follows the codebook and does not affect paper eligibility.

Experiment 2 self-reported creativity: the printed means (3.303 vs 3.279), t(202) = 0.476, d = 0.067, and 95% CI (-0.1608, 0.2631) disagree (p. 6). Correct values require author clarification; this self-report is excluded from criterion 3.

Task-type representation: each experiment includes an alternative uses test (divergent_test) and a product-feature task (idea_generation), documented on pp. 4-5. The existing task.description records both. Any future contrast-level task field is an atlas coding decision requiring no additional source evidence.

External supplementary coverage: the saved PDF ends with the article on p. 10 and has no appended or embedded supplement. Referenced supplementary material and OSF data could not be retrieved because network access was blocked. Additional supplement-only results and details remain unchecked; the main article independently establishes all eligibility criteria.
notes: Outcomes. S1-O1 and S2-O1 (expert-rated creativity) are the primary outcomes. S1-O2 and S2-O2 (expert-rated creative fixation) are mediators scored on the ideas. S1-O3 and S2-O3 (self-reported creativity) are kept with scored_on_output = false, as reconciled c103 keeps self-rated creativity, and they do not affect eligibility. Not listed: the gap between self-reported and expert-rated creativity (Experiment 1: M_human = 1.569, s.d. = 0.899 vs M_LLM = 0.954, s.d. = 0.868; t(202) = 4.972; P < 0.001; p. 5), self-reported inspirational stimulation (five items from Böttger et al.; alpha = 0.968 in Experiment 1 and 0.885 in Experiment 2), and the manipulation checks. Fluency (number of ideas) is not reported, although participants were told to generate as many ideas as possible. Task type: each study crosses an alternative uses test (simple, divergent_test) with a product-feature task (complex, idea_generation). task.type is idea_generation, and task.description names both. Idea pools: the experts rated the LLM and human pools as similarly creative (simple: human 2.200 vs LLM 2.160, t(98) = 0.516, P = 0.607; complex: human 2.180 vs LLM 2.200, t(98) = -0.252, P = 0.801; p. 4). Samples: Each experiment reports 204 recruited and 204 analyzed participants (pp. 4-5; Figs. 2 and 4). Whether recruitment was separate or any people participated in both experiments is not stated; differing demographic summaries do not establish non-overlapping samples. No combined unique-person total is established, and no other paper is named as sharing participants. Primary records: Experiment 1 is ai_vs_active (LLM vs human partner). Experiment 2 is ai_design, with constrained-responsive as the tested configuration and batch-responsive as the default. The ethics approval is dated 01 March 2025, and consent collection began on 29/05/2024 (p. 10). Finalization: The complete markdown conversion, including references and end matter, was read; the PDF passages and figure-only coefficients were checked directly. The sole challenge problem was corrected. All reconciliation.differences entries were marked resolved; the unchanged historical sample-overlap resolution is superseded by final.challenge_resolution. The original reconciliation object remains unchanged. Spec alignment retains the online_rct design classes, records analyzed counts as such, and preserves source.supplement with the limits of verification. Printed statistics are preserved; calculated replacement values and unconfirmed CI/dispersion interpretations were removed from current reported fields and open questions. Read-only urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-025-05867-9 and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/9ckra/files/ both failed with socket-access error WinError 10013. The supplement and posted data were not examined.

challenge_resolution.problem: S2 participants.exclusions, notes, and open_questions asserted separate recruitment without source support; differing demographics do not establish non-overlapping samples.
challenge_resolution.what_changed: Removed the unsupported separate-recruitment and separate-samples claims from S2 participants.exclusions, notes, and open_questions; the design summary and eligibility reason now explicitly retain unknown sample overlap. Each experiment retains its independently documented 204 analyzed participants; no combined unique-person total is inferred. The historical reconciliation object is unchanged as required, but its separate-samples conclusion is superseded by this final decision. The assignment and outcome challenge files contained no problems.

open_items.item: Open question 1: Experiment 1 complex-task F/P inconsistency affects result interpretation, not randomization, analyzed sample size, or output scoring. Author clarification of the printed test is needed.
Open question 2: Cell-level creativity SD/SE labels and possible decimal errors affect effect extraction, not eligibility. Posted participant scores would establish the required dispersions.
Open question 3: Experiment 1 confidence-interval estimands affect effect extraction, not eligibility. Authors must identify which effect each interval describes.

Open question 4: Experiment 2 fixation moderated-mediation index and interval conflict with the prose; the correct values need author clarification. Eligibility does not depend on this mediator result.

Open question 5: Missing arm-level randomized/analyzed counts may be resolved by Supplementary Tables S5-S6. Each experiment already reports 204 analyzed people, so the threshold is met without arm counts.
Open question 6: The reference idea set for fixation scoring in human-partner arms needs author clarification. Expert-rated creativity independently satisfies the output criterion.
Open question 7: Whether participants could message ERNIE Bot may be specified in Supplementary Section S5. Randomized receipt of generative-AI ideas is already established.

Open question 8 and the superseded sample-overlap reconciliation: overlap between experiments is unknown and requires author confirmation. It affects sample dependence, not eligibility, because each experiment independently exceeds the people threshold.

Open question 9: Missing counts, participant-level dispersions and pooled statistics affect primary-effect extraction. Posted participant data would supply the missing information; the paper remains eligible.
Open question 10: Experiment 2 self-report means and inferential statistics disagree and require author clarification. This outcome is not used for eligibility.

Open question 11: Both task types are already established by the source and documented in task.description. Any contrast-level task coding is an atlas representation choice; no additional evidence is needed for eligibility.

Open question 12: The external supplement remains unchecked because publisher and OSF retrieval failed. It is needed to complete coverage of supplementary results and procedural details; main-text evidence already meets all eligibility criteria.
